court: Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit

issues.label: Veterans Court jurisdiction
issues.why: Court must confirm it has statutory authority to review the Board decision challenged.

issues.label: Existence of case or controversy
issues.why: Court must determine whether any live dispute remains after the Board’s PACT Act grant.

issues.label: Mootness after full grant
issues.why: Court must decide whether granting presumptive service connection extinguished the appeal.

issues.label: Scope of relief sought
issues.why: Court must identify whether appellant seeks merits adjudication, remand, or only earlier-effective-date preservation.

issues.label: Downstream effective-date doctrine
issues.why: Court must decide whether effective date is a separate “downstream” issue requiring a new NOD/appeal.

issues.label: Board’s duty to address theories
issues.why: Court must decide whether the Board must adjudicate all reasonably raised service-connection theories (direct vs presumptive).

issues.label: Reasonably raised direct theory
issues.why: Court must determine whether the record and pleadings raised direct service connection for hypertension.

issues.label: Claim vs theory distinction
issues.why: Court must determine whether direct and presumptive are distinct claims or alternative theories within one claim.

issues.label: Board decision adequacy
issues.why: Court must assess whether the Board’s statement to the RO satisfies its obligation to decide the appealed matter.

issues.label: Reasons-or-bases requirement
issues.why: Court must decide whether the Board provided adequate reasons or bases for not adjudicating direct service connection.

issues.label: Board jurisdiction over direct theory
issues.why: Court must confirm whether the Board had jurisdiction to decide direct service connection within the appealed hypertension claim.

issues.label: Duty to maximize benefits
issues.why: Court must consider whether VA must pursue the theory that could yield the earliest effective date and highest benefits.

issues.label: Effective-date legal framework
issues.why: Court must consider how effective dates differ for direct service connection versus liberalizing-law presumptions.

issues.label: PACT Act effective-date limits
issues.why: Court must apply 38 U.S.C. § 5110(g) and 38 C.F.R. § 3.114(a) barring awards prior to Aug. 10, 2022 under the new presumption.

issues.label: Potential earlier effective date
issues.why: Court must determine whether success on direct service connection could legally permit an effective date back to the 2011 claim.

issues.label: Prejudice/harmless error
issues.why: Court must decide whether the Board’s omission caused prejudice by foreclosing or delaying earlier benefits.

issues.label: Appropriate remedy if error
issues.why: Court must decide whether to reverse, vacate-and-remand, or order the Board to adjudicate direct service connection.

issues.label: Permissible remand instructions
issues.why: Court must decide whether it can require the Board (not RO) to address direct service connection and effective-date implications.

issues.label: Finality of Board decision
issues.why: Court must determine what aspects of the Board decision are final and appealable versus matters left for RO implementation.

issues.label: Implicit denial doctrine
issues.why: Court must consider whether the Board implicitly denied direct service connection by granting only presumptive service connection.

issues.label: Bifurcation of theories
issues.why: Court must determine whether the Board may bifurcate presumptive and direct theories and, if so, what procedural safeguards apply.

issues.label: Requirement to remand unadjudicated theory
issues.why: Court must decide whether failure to decide direct theory requires remand rather than dismissal.

issues.label: Board compliance with law changes
issues.why: Court must assess how intervening PACT Act changes affect pending appeals and adjudication duties.

issues.label: Retroactivity of PACT Act
issues.why: Court must address whether and to what extent the PACT Act applies to claims pending before enactment.

issues.label: Interaction with Nehmer rules
issues.why: Court must consider whether any special effective-date rules for herbicide-related claims apply or are displaced for hypertension.

issues.label: Direct service-connection elements
issues.why: If direct theory must be addressed, court must consider evidence of in-service incurrence/aggravation and nexus for hypertension.

issues.label: Competency of lay evidence
issues.why: Court must consider whether the Veteran’s testimony about stress and onset is competent and probative for nexus/onset.

issues.label: Weight of flight-surgeon letter
issues.why: Court must consider whether the submitted medical letter reasonably indicates in-service onset/nexus supporting direct service connection.

issues.label: Duty to assist—medical exam
issues.why: Court must consider whether evidence triggered VA’s obligation to obtain a medical opinion on direct nexus.

issues.label: Continuity/chronic disease rules
issues.why: Court must consider whether hypertension qualifies as a chronic disease and whether presumptive chronic-disease provisions support direct entitlement.

issues.label: Presumption of soundness
issues.why: If onset/aggravation is in question, court must consider whether VA must apply presumption of soundness for each active-duty period.

issues.label: Aggravation during service
issues.why: Court must consider whether hypertension preexisted and was aggravated during the 2003–2005 service period.

issues.label: ACDUTRA/INACDUTRA implications
issues.why: Court must consider whether National Guard service periods affect entitlement based on disease incurred during qualifying duty.

issues.label: Multiple service periods analysis
issues.why: Court must consider which period(s) of service could support direct service connection and how evidence is allocated across them.

issues.label: Standard of review
issues.why: Court must apply the correct standards: legal questions de novo; factual findings under clear-error; reasons-or-bases adequacy.

issues.label: Exhaustion/issue preservation
issues.why: Court must assess whether the direct-theory argument was adequately raised to the Board/Veterans Court for review.

issues.label: Standing despite implementation pending
issues.why: Court must decide whether lack of assigned effective date yet eliminates standing or whether injury exists from failure to adjudicate direct theory.

issues.label: Exceptional mootness exceptions
issues.why: Court must consider exceptions such as capable-of-repetition-yet-evading-review or voluntary cessation in the mootness analysis.

issues.label: Ripeness of direct-theory dispute
issues.why: Court must decide whether the direct-service-connection question is fit for review before RO assigns an effective date.

issues.label: Impact of delay on relief
issues.why: Court must consider whether extraordinary delay affects equitable considerations or supports need for prompt adjudication.

issues.label: Judicial economy vs statutory duty
issues.why: Court must balance efficiency concerns against statutory requirements that the Board decide all questions in the appealed claim.

issues.label: Proper characterization of Board action
issues.why: Court must determine whether the Board’s “informing the RO” is an impermissible advisory opinion or lawful referral.

issues.label: Effect of dismissal on claimant rights
issues.why: Court must consider whether dismissal improperly forces a new appeal path and risks forfeiting the earlier-effective-date opportunity.

issues.label: Remand for statement of reasons
issues.why: Court must consider whether a remand is required solely for adequate explanation even if ultimate entitlement is uncertain.
